key_insight: OmniFabric focuses on generating coherent UV-space textures for 3D garments from a single image, aiming to produce assets that look realistic while staying structurally consistent across the full garment. The key breakthrough is improving texture synthesis so it does not bake in lighting artifacts or break under downstream use.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the challenge of reconstructing production-ready 3D garment textures from a single image. Existing methods often produce textures with inconsistent global structure or embed shadows and environmental illumination, which makes the garments unsuitable for relighting, simulation, and asset production.
method: Synthesizes garment textures directly in UV space to preserve global coherence across the full 3D surface.
Targets texture quality suitable for production workflows, avoiding baked-in lighting and shadow artifacts.
Supports 3D garment reconstruction from sparse input by focusing on coherent appearance generation rather than only local detail completion.
impact: This matters for AI/ML practitioners because it improves the realism and usability of reconstructed 3D assets, especially for fashion, virtual try-on, gaming, and digital content creation. Better UV coherence also makes assets more compatible with relighting, animation, and physical simulation pipelines.

paper_title: OmniFabric: Coherent UV Space Texture Synthesis for 3D Garment Reconstruction
paper_authors: Ding-Jiun Huang, Yuanhao Wang, Cheng Zhang, Hugo Bertiche, Alexandru-Eugen Ichim
